Africa.name: Lion
Africa.description: I am Leo the Lion! I live in sunny grasslands.
Africa.funFact: Lions live in groups called prides!

Africa.name: African Elephant
Africa.description: I have a long trunk and big ears.
Africa.funFact: Elephants can communicate using low-frequency sounds!

Africa.name: Giraffe
Africa.description: I am the tallest land animal!
Africa.funFact: A giraffe's neck is too short to reach the ground!

Africa.name: Zebra
Africa.description: I have black and white stripes.
Africa.funFact: Every zebra has a unique pattern of stripes.

Africa.name: Cheetah
Africa.description: I am the fastest land animal.
Africa.funFact: Cheetahs can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 3 seconds!

Africa.name: Hippopotamus
Africa.description: I love spending time in the water.
Africa.funFact: Hippos secrete a natural sunscreen that is red-colored.

Africa.name: Gorilla
Africa.description: I am a large and powerful primate.
Africa.funFact: Gorillas can learn sign language to communicate with humans.

Africa.name: Meerkat
Africa.description: I am a small mongoose that stands on my hind legs.
Africa.funFact: Meerkats have dark circles around their eyes to reduce sun glare.

Asia.name: Giant Panda
Asia.description: I am a Giant Panda! I eat a lot of bamboo.
Asia.funFact: Pandas can eat up to 38 kilos of bamboo every day!

Asia.name: Bengal Tiger
Asia.description: I am a large wild cat with a striped coat.
Asia.funFact: No two tigers have the same stripes.

Asia.name: Snow Leopard
Asia.description: I live in the snowy mountains.

Asia.name: Orangutan
Asia.description: I am a highly intelligent great ape.
Asia.funFact: Orangutans build a new nest to sleep in every night.

Asia.name: Komodo Dragon
Asia.description: I am the largest living lizard in the world.
Asia.funFact: Komodo dragons can eat up to 80% of their body weight in one meal.

Asia.name: Red Panda
Asia.description: I am a small arboreal mammal.
Asia.funFact: Red pandas use their bushy tails as wraparound blankets in the cold.

North America.name: Bald Eagle
North America.description: I am a bird of prey and a national symbol.
North America.funFact: Bald eagles are not actually bald; their heads are covered in white feathers.

North America.name: Grizzly Bear
North America.description: I am a large brown bear.
North America.funFact: Grizzly bears can run up to 35 mph!

North America.name: Moose
North America.description: I am the largest species in the deer family.
North America.funFact: Moose are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath for up to a minute.

North America.name: Raccoon
North America.description: I am a clever mammal with a masked face.
North America.funFact: Raccoons have highly sensitive front paws that they use to 'see' their food.

North America.name: American Bison
North America.description: I am a large, shaggy bovine.
North America.funFact: Bison are the largest terrestrial animals in North America.

South America.name: Jaguar
South America.description: I am a large cat native to the Americas.
South America.funFact: Jaguars are excellent swimmers and often hunt in the water.

South America.name: Sloth
South America.description: I am known for being very slow.
South America.funFact: Sloths only come down from their trees about once a week.

South America.name: Toucan
South America.description: I am a bird with a large, colorful bill.
South America.funFact: A toucan's bill can be more than half the length of its body.

South America.name: Capybara
South America.description: I am the largest living rodent in the world.
South America.funFact: Capybaras are highly social and often live in groups of 10-20 individuals.

South America.name: Llama
South America.description: I am a domesticated South American camelid.
South America.funFact: Llamas are known to spit when they are annoyed or angry.

Europe.name: Red Fox
Europe.description: I am a small, cunning mammal.
Europe.funFact: Red foxes can hear a watch ticking from 40 yards away.

Europe.name: Hedgehog
Europe.description: I am a small, spiny mammal.
Europe.funFact: Hedgehogs have about 5,000 to 7,000 spines on their backs.

Europe.name: Gray Wolf
Europe.description: I am a large wild canine.
Europe.funFact: Wolves live and hunt in packs of 6 to 10 animals.

Europe.name: Brown Bear
Europe.description: I am a large bear species.
Europe.funFact: During winter hibernation, a brown bear's heart rate drops from 40 to 8 beats per minute.

Europe.name: Reindeer
Europe.description: I am a species of deer native to Arctic regions.
Europe.funFact: Reindeer are the only deer species where both males and females grow antlers.

Oceania.name: Kangaroo
Oceania.description: I am a large marsupial that hops.

Oceania.name: Koala
Oceania.funFact: Koalas can sleep for up to 22 hours a day!

Oceania.name: Platypus
Oceania.description: I am a unique, egg-laying mammal.
Oceania.funFact: The platypus does not have a stomach.

Oceania.name: Emu
Oceania.description: I am the second-tallest living bird.
Oceania.funFact: Emus cannot fly, but they can run at speeds up to 30 mph.

Oceania.name: Kiwi
Oceania.description: I am a flightless bird native to New Zealand.
Oceania.funFact: Kiwis have their nostrils at the very tip of their long beaks.

Antarctica.name: Emperor Penguin
Antarctica.description: I am the tallest and heaviest of all living penguin species.
Antarctica.funFact: Emperor penguins can dive to depths of over 500 meters!

Antarctica.name: Leopard Seal
Antarctica.description: I am a large and formidable predator.
Antarctica.funFact: Leopard seals use their powerful jaws to catch penguins and other seals.

Antarctica.name: Orca
Antarctica.description: I am a toothed whale and the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family.
Antarctica.funFact: Orcas are highly intelligent and have complex social structures.

Antarctica.name: Snow Petrel
Antarctica.description: I am one of only three birds that breed exclusively in Antarctica.
Antarctica.funFact: Snow petrels are completely white with black eyes and a small black bill.

Antarctica.name: Wandering Albatross
Antarctica.description: I am a large seabird with the longest wingspan of any living bird.
Antarctica.funFact: An albatross can fly for thousands of miles without flapping its wings.
